reviewer_scope: Visual inspection only, batches 10 through 35 inclusive
method: Actually opened every batch-10.png through batch-35.png with view_image and visually inspected each 300x250 source rendering and native game rendering.
Read all 248 exact batch-manifest prompts and compared visible subjects, period equipment, materials, diagrams and exclusions against README heraldry and palette-guidance rules.
Opened 24 selected source PNGs using view_image detail=original, including every asset with a new finding and every additional technical candidate in scope.
Compared avian_will_never_fall with the native AVI_neutrality.png flag reference.
Used Python/Pillow solely to create inspection contact sheets and crops; original assets and native exports were never edited.
Viewed all seven technical candidates at source size and on dark/light source+native contact sheets. Viewed a separate full-resolution top/bottom crop for technical_college.
Rechecked all 248 source paths and SHA256 hashes after the visual review; no changes from the initial reviewed snapshot.

review_standards.miniatures: Accepted symbolic object arrangements, simplified machinery, diagram counters and ordinary small details when the intended subject remains clear at 99x86.
review_standards.text: Distinguished meaningful dot tables, geometric diagrams and intentionally legible textbook letters/numerals from pseudo-writing.
review_standards.alpha: Did not equate mesh, gate or machinery openings with transparency defects. Raw transparent-image edge colors were tested in normal alpha composites before treating them as defects.
review_standards.scope_limit: This is a source/composite visual audit, not an in-game runtime approval or a replacement for the separate technical audit. Only listed source hashes are covered; future replacements require re-review.

findings.observation: Dominant control console is a wide flat green display with a combined graph/flowchart and rows of square control buttons; it reads as a modern digital process-control terminal in both sheet and source.
findings.basis: HOI4/EaW period equipment context; laboratory console should use period instruments. The batch prompt did not explicitly prohibit screens, so this is an art-direction correction rather than a claimed explicit prompt violation.
findings.corrective_prompt: Retain the grain silo and surveying instrument. Replace the wide digital monitor with a 1930s enamel console containing three round needle gauges, a paper chart recorder and chunky bakelite switches. No luminous display, screen GUI or added wheat wreath. Steel machinery, matte straw grain, transparent exterior; readable at 99x86.
